picks.name: Resident Evil
picks.why: Zach Cregger's new take on the survival-horror franchise: a hapless courier is trapped in a hospital outbreak. Expect sharp, fast-moving horror with an ordinary guy in way over his head.

picks.name: Talk to Me
picks.why: Teens turn a séance hand into a party game and get hooked on possession. It's peer pressure and grief made literal, with nasty stakes that keep climbing.

picks.name: Thoroughbreds
picks.why: Two estranged rich-kid friends in Connecticut casually talk themselves into murdering a stepfather. A deadpan, chilly dark comedy about people calmly going along with something monstrous.

picks.name: Our Hero, Balthazar
picks.why: A rich New York teen trying to impress his activist crush follows an online contact to Texas, thinking he can stop a mass act of violence. It's a dark comedy thriller about internet-age self-delusion that keeps getting more uncomfortable.

picks.name: Ready or Not
picks.why: A new bride's wedding night turns into a deadly game of hide-and-seek with her rich in-laws. It's a pitch-black comedy thriller about a polite family that goes along with something monstrous, and it is funny and tense all the way through.

picks.name: Marty Supreme
picks.why: A hustler chasing table-tennis glory careens from one bad decision to the next. The anxiety never lets up, it's often very funny, and there's always something at stake.

picks.name: Clayface
picks.why: A rising Hollywood star loses his face and his identity to a scientific experiment and turns into a monster bent on revenge. Body horror and a revenge story in one, with an unsparing look at vanity and fame.

picks.name: Hard Candy
picks.why: A teenage girl turns the tables on a man she meets online, and it becomes a tense two-hander of revenge and control. A lesser-known, sharply made shocker from a woman's point of view, with a merciless last act.

picks.name: The Handmaiden
picks.why: Park Chan-wook's lush, erotic con-game thriller set in 1930s Korea, where a maid and an heiress play a long game of double-crosses against the men scheming over them. Twisted, beautifully controlled, and built toward a deeply satisfying revenge payoff.

picks.name: The Vanishing
picks.why: A Dutch thriller about a man searching for his missing girlfriend and the calm, ordinary family man who took her. The film tightens slowly to one of the most chilling endings ever filmed.

new.name: Tuner
new.why: A piano tuner with painfully sensitive hearing finds he can crack safes, and his life slides into crime. A precise, unusual thriller built around one strange skill.

new.name: Dust Bunny
new.why: Bryan Fuller's debut feature: a girl hires the hitman next door to kill the monster under her bed. A strange, stylish dark fairy tale played completely straight.

new.name: Lo dejamos acá
new.why: A disillusioned psychoanalyst starts secretly meddling in his patients' lives, with great results, until one patient pushes back. A dark comedy about a quiet abuse of power.

new.name: The Storm
new.why: A lavish 45th-birthday dinner at a remote Swedish estate, with a ferocious storm on the way. Scandinavian social comedy where a sealed-off group of privileged people turns on each other.

new.name: Redux Redux
new.why: A mother jumps between parallel universes to kill her daughter's murderer again and again, and loses a little more of herself each time. Pulpy, inventive revenge with a dark core.

new.name: Pillion
new.why: A shy man becomes the submissive of an enigmatic biker in this British comedy. It treats an extreme power dynamic with a dry, totally straight face.

new.name: Carolina Caroline
new.why: A young woman joins a charming con man on a crime spree across the Southeast. A lovers-on-the-run story with an edge of danger.

new.name: Never After Dark
new.why: A traveling psychic investigates a powerful entity in a remote house and finds the real threat comes from somewhere unexpected. Supernatural horror with a mystery at its center.

new.name: Unabomber
new.why: A crime drama tracing a Harvard student's path from psychological experiments to a deadly bombing campaign, alongside the FBI hunt that caught him.

new.name: The Rivals of Amziah King
new.why: A beekeeper who anchors his small community reunites with his former foster daughter while threats close in on his honey business. It's a slow-burn rural crime thriller with menace under a folksy surface.

dread.name: Bring Her Back
dread.why: From the Philippou brothers: two siblings are placed with a foster mother whose grief has turned into something monstrous. Relentless and cruel horror that keeps tightening to the end.

dread.name: Speak No Evil
dread.why: In the Danish original, a polite couple spends a weekend with a family they met on holiday and keeps excusing behavior that grows steadily worse. Its ending is famously brutal.

dread.name: Longlegs
dread.why: An FBI agent hunts a satanic serial killer in this cold, precise horror film. The dread builds slowly, and it ends somewhere truly upsetting.

dread.name: Enemy
dread.why: Denis Villeneuve's thriller about a man who finds his exact double. Jake Gyllenhaal stars in a cold, controlled puzzle with one of the most unsettling final shots in modern film.

dread.name: Mother
dread.why: Bong Joon-ho's thriller about a mother who will do anything to clear her son of murder. Dark, darkly funny in places, and ending on a devastating turn.

dread.name: Memories of Murder
dread.why: Bong Joon-ho's serial-killer investigation in 1980s rural Korea, where incompetence and cruelty pile up alongside the bodies. Its ending is unforgettable.

dread.name: Goodnight Mommy
dread.why: In the Austrian original, twin boys become convinced the bandaged woman who came home from surgery isn't their mother. Austere, cruel and extremely tense.

dread.name: The Chaser
dread.why: A disgraced cop turned pimp hunts the serial killer who has taken one of his women. A Korean thriller that is breathless, brutal and doesn't flinch.

dread.name: Burning
dread.why: Lee Chang-dong's slow-burn mystery about a delivery boy, the woman he likes and the smiling rich man who may have made her disappear. The menace keeps growing until a sudden release at the end.

dread.name: Funny Games
dread.why: Michael Haneke's shot-for-shot English remake of his own film: two polite young men take a family hostage at their lake house. It is clinical and merciless, and the director is fully in charge.

deadpan.name: Bernie
deadpan.why: Based on a true story: a beloved small-town Texas mortician kills a hated widow, and the town would rather he got away with it. Richard Linklater plays it completely straight.

deadpan.name: The Lobster
deadpan.why: Yorgos Lanthimos's satire in which single people get 45 days to find a partner or be turned into animals. Everyone delivers absurd cruelty in a flat monotone.

deadpan.name: Happiness
deadpan.why: Todd Solondz's interlocking portrait of suburban New Jersey, where ordinary people hide monstrous secrets. It is unbearably deadpan.

deadpan.name: Force Majeure
deadpan.why: A father runs from an avalanche and leaves his family behind, and the rest of their ski holiday turns into a quiet trial. Ruben Östlund's precise, excruciating comedy.

deadpan.name: Kinds of Kindness
deadpan.why: Yorgos Lanthimos's three-part film about people who give up everything to please those who control them. Cruel, strange and deadpan throughout.

deadpan.name: Fargo
deadpan.why: The Coen brothers' crime story about a car salesman whose plan to have his wife kidnapped falls apart. Murder plays out against Minnesota politeness.

deadpan.name: To Die For
deadpan.why: Nicole Kidman plays a small-town weather girl who will do anything to get on TV, including talking teenagers into murder. A sly satire played cool.

deadpan.name: World's Greatest Dad
deadpan.why: After his awful son dies in an embarrassing accident, a failed writer fakes a suicide note, and the whole school embraces the lie. Bobcat Goldthwait's pitch-black comedy.

deadpan.name: Sightseers
deadpan.why: A mild British couple on a caravan holiday start killing anyone who annoys them. Ben Wheatley plays the murders as small domestic matters.

deadpan.name: Wild Tales
deadpan.why: An Argentine anthology of six stories in which ordinary people pushed by small slights escalate to wrecked cars, poison and a wedding that turns into a massacre. It is pitch-black and very funny, and every story ends on a sharp punchline.

deepcuts.name: Cure
deepcuts.why: Kiyoshi Kurosawa's Japanese thriller about a detective chasing murders committed by ordinary people who don't know why they did it. Hypnotic and deeply unsettling.

deepcuts.name: Compliance
deepcuts.why: Based on a true story: a prank caller posing as a cop talks fast-food staff into abusing a coworker. A study of ordinary people obeying something monstrous.

deepcuts.name: Confessions
deepcuts.why: Tetsuya Nakashima's Japanese film about a teacher who calmly tells her class that two students killed her daughter, and that she has already taken revenge. Icy and stylish.

deepcuts.name: Snowtown
deepcuts.why: Based on Australia's worst serial killings: a charismatic neighbor draws a teenager into his circle of killers. Quiet, horrifying and real.

deepcuts.name: Kill List
deepcuts.why: Ben Wheatley's British film about two ex-soldiers turned hitmen whose latest job is getting stranger. It moves from kitchen-sink drama into nightmare, with a bleak final turn.

deepcuts.name: Cheap Thrills
deepcuts.why: A broke father meets an old friend at a bar, where a rich couple starts paying them for ever-worse dares. Escalation turned into a dark comedy.

deepcuts.name: Big Bad Wolves
deepcuts.why: In this Israeli thriller, a vigilante cop and a grieving father kidnap a suspected child killer. Brutal and unexpectedly funny, with a final shot that bites.

deepcuts.name: Dogtooth
deepcuts.why: Yorgos Lanthimos's Greek breakthrough about parents who keep their grown children sealed in a compound of invented rules. Cruel, deadpan and very strange.

deepcuts.name: Man Bites Dog
deepcuts.why: A Belgian mockumentary in which a film crew follows a charming serial killer and slowly becomes his accomplice. Pitch-black satire played straight.

deepcuts.name: The Hunt
deepcuts.why: A Danish kindergarten teacher is falsely accused, and his small town turns on him. Thomas Vinterberg's portrait of a community's cruelty is agonizingly tense.

series.name: The Beast in Me
series.why: A grieving author becomes obsessed with her charming neighbor, whose wife disappeared. A slow-burn psychological thriller about suspicion, obsession and a man who may be a monster.

series.name: Yellowjackets
series.why: A high school girls' soccer team stranded in the wilderness turns on itself, and the survivors are still hiding what happened decades later. Teen cruelty, social pecking orders and psychological horror with real stakes.

series.name: The Price of Confession
series.why: A woman accused of killing her husband is offered a deal by a mysterious stranger: to prove her innocence, she must commit a murder. A twisty Korean psychological thriller built on moral compromise.

series.name: Dexter: Resurrection
series.why: The serial killer with a code wakes from a coma and heads to New York to find his son as his past closes in. A darkly funny crime thriller that keeps the suspense going episode to episode.

series.name: Dear X
series.why: A woman hides behind a mask to escape her past and climbs to power, destroying everyone in her way. A twisted, stylish story of a female antihero's revenge.

series.name: Fargo
series.why: An anthology of Midwestern crime stories in which ordinary people slide into monstrous acts. Deadpan, violent and tightly plotted each season.

series.name: Baby Reindeer
series.why: A struggling comedian's kindness to a stranger turns into a years-long stalking nightmare. Told unflinchingly and impossible to stop watching.

series.name: Mindhunter
series.why: David Fincher's series about the FBI agents who invented criminal profiling by interviewing serial killers. Calm, chilling conversations with real monsters.
